messages:
Carlos (customer): Hey team — we started seeing intermittent SSE disconnects across a few tenants. Clients get ~15-30s of streaming then a reconnect occurs; when they resume, final tokens sometimes missing or duplicated. Happened to three different customers. Uploaded pcap: s3://redwood-support/pcaps/pcap-1934567890-carlos.pcap. trace_id=trace-0x4f7a

Aisha (support): Ugh, thanks for reporting. Can you paste the exact curl/SDK pattern you use and how resume tokens are posted? Also which SDK version? :eyes:

Carlos (customer): Node SDK v2.3.1 (planning to try v2.4). Pattern: open SSE with Authorization: Bearer <short-lived JWT>. On disconnect we POST to /v1/stream/resume with resume_token. curl repro: ```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-medium"
```
When we call resume sometimes we get 200 but only last ~20 tokens arrive; other times we see repeated fragments with overlapping token ids.

Ben (support): I grabbed the pcap and server logs. The resume POST sometimes returns HTTP/2 401 and immediately after we see TCP FINs. Server-side logs show token validation failures on resume requests (timestamp out-of-range). Local pcap: /mnt/support/pcaps/pcap-1934567890-carlos.pcap

Sam (SRE): Adding context from infra: around 2026-11-03T17:05:12Z we had an experimental change in the edge proxy (proxy-reaper) that tightened stream idle/heartbeat behavior. It closed some long-running connections aggressively. Combined with short-lived JWTs (~30s TTL) this can cause a race: client reconnects and resume token appears expired at the auth layer -> resume rejected -> original connection still pushes trailing events then FIN -> client retries and receives overlapping fragments leading to duplicate event ids. Matches trace trace-0x4f7a.

Carlos (customer): Any mitigations we can do quickly? We can't extend token TTLs on our side. Billing duplicates are a blocker for us.

Aisha (support): Short-term recommendations: 1) increase client-side reconnect backoff and add application-level dedupe for the last N event ids; 2) only POST to /v1/stream/resume after you see the connection closed or a final event; 3) try SDK v2.4 which includes improved resume jitter and safer resume semantics.

Ben (support): In the logs I see entries like: ```
[2026-11-03T17:05:12Z] resume_handler trace=trace-0x4f7a token=abc123 validate_error="timestamp out-of-range"
[2026-11-03T17:05:12Z] connection_manager conn=conn-43 status=closing reason=auth_failed
```
I filed ENG-7893 for runtime investigation. Also an alert fired: ingest-bot: alert: sse_resume_fail_rate for namespace=prod-support increased by 540% in 5m (metric sse.resume.fail.rate -> 0.054).

Sam (SRE): Hypothesis: interaction of JWT TTL=30s, proxy heartbeat=20s (experimental), and resume_token validation window=60s caused inconsistent acceptance of resume tokens. That plus late-arriving fragment delivery produces duplicate event ids and sometimes truncated final segments. We also noticed duplicate IDs can cause double billing if clients ack/retry aggressively.

Carlos (customer): Can you stop double billing on your side while we fix?

Aisha (support): Short-term: please add dedupe on your ingest side by event id. We're going to apply a temporary ops change to widen resume validation window to 90s for your org (org-carlos) while we implement a server-side mitigation. I filed OPS-1422.

Ben (support): Repro steps we used in lab (for eng):
1) Run a JWT issuer with TTL=30s
2) Start an edge proxy configured with heartbeat_timeout=20s
3) Client opens SSE and requests a long-running generation (>512 tokens)
4) Kill the proxy pod after ~15s to simulate half-delivery
5) Client immediately POSTs /v1/stream/resume with same resume_token -> observe 401
6) Client retries resume a couple seconds later -> sometimes 200 but last chunk incomplete -> overlapping fragments produce duplicate ids
Commands: ```
# repro runner
node reproduce/sse-resume.js --token-ttl=30 --proxy-heartbeat=20 --prompt=very_long_prompt.txt
# capture network
tcpdump -w /tmp/pcap-1934567890.pcap -i any port 443
```
We uploaded a small repro bundle: s3://redwood-support/repros/sse-resume-flake-1934567890.tar.gz

Sam (SRE): Engineering plan: short patch to extend resume validation window to 90s for affected orgs and roll back the heartbeat experiment on edge for 48h (ETA ~2h). Medium-term: add server-side idempotency keyed by resume_token+request_id to avoid double counting on retries (ENG-7901). Long-term: redesign resume protocol to include explicit resume_ACK and tolerate mid-token key rotations.

Aisha (support): Observability checklist for follow-ups: collect trace ids (trace-0x4f7a), metrics (sse.resume.attempts, sse.resume.fail.rate, sse.session.disconnect.count, sse.partial-segment.count), and logs (resume_handler, connection_manager, proxy_reaper, auth-token-rotate). If you see the issue again, attach fresh pcap and new trace id.

Ben (support): I added a temporary dashboard and alert: alerts->sse_resume_high_jitter (trigger: p95 reconnect < 40s AND fail_rate > 0.02). I've also uploaded the pcap and repro to eng.

deploy-bot: deploy: prod/edge-proxy rollback of heartbeat-experiment -> success (deploy id d-98123)

Aisha (support): Ops change applied to staging; rolling patch to prod now to widen resume clock window for org-carlos. I'll post back once prod change is live. :thumbsup:

Aisha (support): Patch is live in prod. Can you run the same flow and confirm within 30 minutes whether you still see partial segments or duplicated billing? If so, please share new pcap and trace id.

Carlos (customer): Confirmed — ran two runs with SDK v2.4 and our dedupe; no duplicate billing and no partial segments observed. We'll keep monitoring and will attach anything new if it recurs. Thanks all! :pray:

Ben (support): Closing loop — ENG-7893 and ENG-7901 created for follow-ups; postmortem task added to review token TTL guidance and update SDK resume docs.
